原创示例：An initialization-centered regularizer cancels the iterate-dependent terms in the two players’ regret bounds. This yields an expected gap guarantee for averaged iterates without a prescribed projection radius, including stochastic gradients whose second moments grow with the iterates.

counterexamples.finding: Unbounded gradients means structured linear growth/finite conditional second moments, not arbitrary noise/objectives. Gap for averaged iterates against finite adaptive comparators is not last-iterate convergence or almost-sure bounded paths. Algorithm knows growth constant/geometry/horizon for tuning but not comparator norm; MDP simulator access at any state-action with SA+1 samples/iteration differs from online trajectory RL. Bias bound remains in guarantee although not supplied to algorithm.

MDP policy bias/comparators require the stated stationary-distribution/bias existence setting, not all arbitrary multichain or periodic problems. B^4 S^2 A^2 log(SA)/eps² queries vs B^4 SA log(SA)/eps² iterations. No empirical training stability or wallclock data, no universal optimum over S/A. Related-work comparison is the authors’ positioning, not an independent audit of cited papers.

Intro baseline ascent sign and prox squared-norm factors inconsistent with later closed form; Eq4 prints square of expected norm while proof uses expected squared norm; A.2 regularized-objective half factors inconsistent. p17 mixing-time definition t≤1 missing intended contraction threshold; p20 sum dropsT then final averaging. p23 variance inequality for arbitrary norm needs justification/constant (unbiasedness alone gives Hilbert variance identity), and ghost comparator called independent though data-adaptive; deterministic pathwise regret may avoid independence. Clarifications retained, not proof certification/refutation or writing rules.
